models._description: (extension) adds quiz_id/quiz_ids + per-visitor quiz state (is_quiz_completed, quiz_points)
(extension) stores the visitor's quiz result (quiz_completed, quiz_points)

behavioral_notes.observation: The public submit route is the module's core write. It _fetch_track(track_id) (parent-module ACL/website check), then track._get_event_track_visitors(force_create=True) which resolves the caller's website.visitor (force-creating one for anonymous users) or partner and returns/creates the event.track.visitor row. It reads the submitted answer_ids as sudo (event.quiz.answer is not public-readable) via _get_quiz_answers_details, which guards completeness (len(user_answers.question_id) must equal track.quiz_questions_count, else error 'quiz_incomplete') and SCORES the attempt as points = sum(answer.awarded_points) over the chosen answers. It then writes quiz_completed=True and quiz_points=points onto the event.track.visitor and returns per-question correction (correct_answer text, is_correct, awarded_points, comment). So an anonymous attendee accumulates gamification points on a real event.track.visitor row. Not visible in metadata.

Scoring is server-side and single-attempt: event_track_quiz_submit short-circuits with {'error': 'track_quiz_done'} if the resolved event.track.visitor.quiz_completed is already True, so a visitor cannot re-submit to farm points. Answers and points are fetched/computed server-side as sudo (the browser only POSTs answer_ids), so the client cannot dictate the score, and the completeness check forces every question to be answered. The /event_track/quiz/reset route clears quiz_completed/quiz_points back to 0 but is gated: it raises werkzeug Forbidden unless the user has_group('event.group_event_manager') OR the quiz's repeatable ('Unlimited Tries') flag is set, so a normal attendee can only retake when the organizer explicitly allows it. Pure code semantics, invisible to metadata.

Points live on event.quiz.answer.awarded_points (Integer, per-answer). event.quiz.question.awarded_points is a compute summing its answers' awarded_points, and correct_answer_id is a compute = answer_ids.filtered(is_correct). A @api.constrains('answer_ids') _check_answers_integrity enforces data validity at write time: each question must have exactly 1 correct answer and at least 2 answers total (else ValidationError), guaranteeing every quiz question is gradeable. event.quiz.repeatable governs retakes. These compute/constraint semantics are not derivable from field metadata.

The track page render is personalised per viewer: _compute_quiz_data (@api.depends_context('uid')) resolves the current website.visitor (_get_visitor_from_request) and/or logged partner, sudo search_reads event.track.visitor for (track, quiz_completed, quiz_points) and projects is_quiz_completed / quiz_points onto the track for the current user only (public + no-visitor -> 0/False). This couples the public track page to per-visitor event.track.visitor state so the quiz interaction widget knows whether to lock itself. Python logic, not metadata.

The community/leaderboard routes aggregate the gamification scores into a ranking: _get_leaderboard sudo _read_groups event.track.visitor over the event's tracks (visitor_id set, quiz_points>0) summing quiz_points:sum per visitor, ordered DESC, building positions and a top3, then highlighting the current visitor's row (current_visitor_position). _get_community_leaderboard_render_values paginates 30/page (max 5 pager pages) and can auto-scroll to the caller's position. This cross-track points roll-up per attendee is the community-engagement payoff of the quizzes and exists only in controller code.

2 JS files / 1 XML template, no OWL components: the quiz UX is a website public.interaction Quiz (static selector '.o_quiz_main') extracting questions/answers from server-rendered DOM, posting checked radio answer_ids to /event_track/quiz/submit, then decorating each answer (check/times icon, awarded-points badge, comment) and re-rendering the karma/validation box from the JSON correction; onResetQuizClick POSTs /event_track/quiz/reset. A second Leaderboard interaction simply smooth-scrolls the current visitor's leaderboard row into view. Entirely client-side, outside Python metadata.

it_architecture.application: website_event_track_quiz (gamified-quiz extension on the event-track website experience)
software_services: /event_track/quiz/submit (jsonrpc, public) -- score answers + write event.track.visitor (quiz_completed, quiz_points)
/event_track/quiz/reset (jsonrpc, public) -- clear a visitor's quiz result (gated by repeatable / event_manager)
logical_data_erm: event.quiz.question -> event.quiz (quiz_id, cascade); event.quiz.answer -> event.quiz.question (question_id, cascade)
event.track.visitor -> event.track / website.visitor / res.partner (carries quiz_completed, quiz_points)
leaderboard: event.track.visitor.quiz_points:sum grouped by website.visitor over event.track_ids
information_flows: depends: website_profile, website_event_track (-> website_event, event, website)
side-effect: POST /event_track/quiz/submit -> _get_event_track_visitors force-creates website.visitor + event.track.visitor, scores answers, writes quiz_completed/quiz_points
side-effect: POST /event_track/quiz/reset -> event.track.visitor.write(quiz_completed=False, quiz_points=0) when repeatable or event_manager
read-flow: event.track._compute_quiz_data (depends_context uid) -> per-viewer event.track.visitor projection onto the track page
aggregation: community leaderboard -> _read_group event.track.visitor quiz_points:sum per visitor across the event's tracks
frontend_components: public.interaction Quiz (.o_quiz_main): submit answers to /event_track/quiz/submit, decorate correction, render karma/validation, reset via /event_track/quiz/reset
public.interaction Leaderboard (.o_wevent_quiz_leaderboard .o_wevent_quiz_scroll_to): smooth-scroll current visitor row into view

capabilities: Author Track Quizzes (quiz, questions, answers with per-answer points)
Gamified Self-Assessment on a Talk/Track (answer + immediate scored correction)
Attendee Points Accumulation per Track (quiz_points on event.track.visitor)
One-Attempt / Repeatable Quiz Gating (anti-cheat completion + optional retry)
Event Community Leaderboard / Ranking (cross-track points roll-up per visitor)
value_streams: Engage-and-Score: attendee opens a track page -> answers the quiz -> server scores answers (sum awarded_points) -> event.track.visitor stamped quiz_completed/quiz_points -> correction shown -> points roll up into the event leaderboard ranking
policies: 3 ir.model.access rules: event.quiz / .question / .answer are read-write-create-unlink for event.group_event_user only (authoring restricted to event staff)
anti-cheat: server-side single attempt -- submit refused once quiz_completed is True; score computed server-side as sudo, never trusted from the client
data-integrity constraint: each quiz question must have exactly 1 correct answer and >=2 answers (_check_answers_integrity)
reset policy: a visitor may retake only if quiz.repeatable ('Unlimited Tries') is set, otherwise only event managers can reset
leaderboard scope: only visitor-linked event.track.visitor rows with quiz_points>0 are ranked
stakeholders: Event Attendee / Website Visitor (quiz taker, public user)
Registered Attendee (res.partner / website.visitor on the leaderboard)
Event Speaker / Content Author (event.group_event_user authoring quizzes)
metrics: event.track.visitor.quiz_points (points earned per attendee per track)
leaderboard standings: quiz_points:sum per visitor across an event's tracks

classification.apqc_category: 3.0 Market and Sell Products and Services
classification.rationale: website_event_track_quiz is a community-engagement extension layered on the website_event value network: it inherits the mediating-technology logic (Stabell & Fjeldstad) of its parents rather than transforming inputs into outputs. Its reason to exist is to deepen the connection between an open population of attendees and the event's content -- it bolts a gamified quiz onto each talk/track, lets anonymous and logged visitors answer and earn points (quiz_points on event.track.visitor), and rolls those points up into a per-event community leaderboard that ranks participants. That is membership/mediation value (engagement, scoring, and ranking of a shared pool of attendees around shared content), the network signature, not a sequential chain (no input->output good is produced) nor case-by-case shop problem-solving. activity_class is primary because it is a customer-facing audience-engagement / event-marketing feature on the public website, not a back-office support function. apqc_category 3.0 Market and Sell Products and Services is the closest PCF home, matching the website_event / website_event_track lineage: the motion is engaging and retaining a marketed event's audience (demand-side market/sell), not post-sale customer service (6.0). strategy is null (human-only).

standard_capabilities: attach a quiz (event.quiz) with ordered questions and multiple-choice answers to any event track
per-answer point weighting (awarded_points) with exactly-one-correct-answer validation
public, single-attempt quiz taking with immediate scored correction (check/cross, points badge, per-answer comment)
per-attendee points stored on event.track.visitor for both anonymous (website.visitor) and logged users
optional 'Unlimited Tries' (repeatable) retake, with event-manager override reset
per-event community leaderboard ranking visitors by total quiz points, paginated, with current-visitor highlight
typical_fits: conferences / trainings adding interactive knowledge-check quizzes to recorded or live talks
gamified audience engagement with a points leaderboard to drive session attendance/competition
free self-assessment after a session with instant feedback and explanatory comments
common_gaps: karma / badges depth: the quiz template surfaces karma data attributes, but full karma awarding lives in website_profile / gamification glue, not here
quiz analytics / per-question success-rate reporting beyond raw points
richer question types (multi-select, free-text, ordering) -- only single-correct multiple-choice is standard
certification / pass-fail thresholds and time limits are not part of this module

open_questions: Exact karma/gamification coupling with website_profile: the quiz template surfaces quizKarmaMax/Won/Gain data attributes, but where karma is actually awarded to the partner (vs. the local quiz_points on event.track.visitor) was not traced in this module.
Interplay of reset-then-resubmit with the leaderboard sum in a live DB: reset zeroes the event.track.visitor row (no historization of prior points observed).
Runtime row counts for event.quiz / event.track.visitor with quiz_points were not captured (extract_runtime.sh not run).
